intro: Muslims believe the words of the Qur'an came to a man named Muhammad. Who was he? Where did he live? This unit tells his story. It tells it the way Muslims tell it.
You will visit a hot desert city called Mecca. You will meet a boy who lost his parents. He cared for sheep. Muslims say an angel came to him in a cave. The angel said, "Read!"
By the end, you will be able to tell the story in order. You will know the words prophet, angel and revelation. You will know why Muslims say "peace be upon him."
bigQuestion: How do Muslims tell the story of Muhammad and the first words of the Qur'an?

timeline.t: Muslim tradition says Muhammad is born in Mecca.
His mother dies; his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib cares for him.
His grandfather dies; his uncle Abu Talib raises him.
He cares for sheep and travels with the caravans.
People in Mecca call him al-Amin, the trustworthy.
He marries Khadijah, a trader in Mecca.
In the cave of Hira, Muslims say the angel Jibril says, "Read!"
He runs home afraid; Khadijah wraps him in a blanket and comforts him.
Muslims say Khadijah is the first to believe the message.
Muslims believe more words come for about 23 years; friends learn them by heart.
Muslims say his friends gather the words into one book, the Qur'an.

words.d: a city in the desert of Arabia where Muslims say Muhammad was born
a very old building shaped like a box in the middle of Mecca; Muslims believe it is a house for God
a long line of camels or people traveling together with things to sell
a child whose mother and father have died
honest and safe to count on; a person who keeps their word
the angel Muslims believe brought the words of the Qur'an to Muhammad; Gabriel in English
words Muslims believe God sent down to Muhammad through the angel Jibril
a person who brings a message from God, as Muslims, Jews and Christians believe

choices: A long line of camels carrying goods
test.why: Caravans of camels carried goods to and from Mecca.

test.q: Who raised Muhammad after his grandfather died?
test.why: Muslim tradition says his uncle Abu Talib cared for him.
People in Mecca called him al-Amin, the trustworthy, because he was honest.
Khadijah ran a trading business and became Muhammad's wife.

test.q: Where do Muslims say the angel came to Muhammad?
test.why: Muslim tradition says the angel Jibril came to him in the cave of Hira.
Iqra is the Arabic word for Read! Muslims say it was the first word.

test.q: Who do Muslims say was the first to believe?
test.why: Muslims say Khadijah, his wife, believed first.

write.prompt: Draw and tell: How do Muslims say the first words of the Qur'an came? Use the first lines of surah 96, the story of the blanket, and surah 73:1. Tell what each one says and what Muslims say it means.
tips: Say "Muslims believe" or "Muslim tradition says" when you tell the story.
Name the surah when you use its words, like surah 96.
Tell the story in order: the cave, the word Read, the run home, the blanket.
Use the words prophet, angel and revelation.

title: Muhammad and the First Words

chapters.title: A Boy in Mecca
chapters.bigQuestion: Who was Muhammad, and what was his life like before the Qur'an?

story.title: The Camels Come to Town
story.kicker: A boy sits on a rock and watches a long line of camels walk into a city in the sand.
paragraphs: The sun is hot. The ground is dry sand and gray rock. A boy sits on a big stone at the edge of town. He shades his eyes with his hand. Far away, he sees a cloud of dust. The camels are coming.

The camels walk in a long line. Each one carries heavy bags. Inside the bags are cloth, dates, spices and things to sell. Men walk beside the camels. They have come a long way. They are tired and glad to see the town.
The town is called Mecca. In the middle of Mecca stands a building shaped like a big box. People come from far away to see it. The boy has seen it many times. He lives here.
Muslims tell this story about a boy named Muhammad. They say he grew up in Mecca long, long ago. They tell his story with love. In this chapter, you will hear how they tell it.
story.think: What would you like to see if a line of camels came to your town?

lessons.title: Mecca and the Big Box
lessons.mainIdea: Mecca is a desert city with a square building called the Kaaba in the middle.
reading: *Mecca* is a city in a hot, dry land. It has sand, rocks and hills. It does not rain much. Long ago, people found a well there. So people came to live near the water.
In the middle of Mecca is a building shaped like a box. It is called the *Kaaba*. Muslims believe it is a house built for God. It is very old.
Today Mecca is in a country called Saudi Arabia. Millions of Muslims travel there each year. They walk around the Kaaba together.

words.d: a city in the desert of Arabia where Muslims say Muhammad was born
a very old building shaped like a box in the middle of Mecca; Muslims believe it is a house for God

look.title: Look at the Kaaba
look.text: Look at a big building in the middle of a wide, flat yard. It is shaped like a cube, like a giant box. It is covered in black cloth. Around it, thousands of people walk slowly in a circle. They all move the same way.
look.prompt: What do you notice about how the people move around the Kaaba?

check.q: What is Mecca?
check.why: Mecca is a city in a hot, dry land in Arabia.

check.q: What shape is the Kaaba?
check.why: The Kaaba is a building shaped like a box, or a cube.

check.q: Why did people first come to live in Mecca?
choices: Because it had a well with water
check.why: In a dry land, a well with water is a reason to stay. People settled near it.

lessons.title: Camels and Caravans
lessons.mainIdea: Mecca was a trading city, and lines of camels called caravans came and went.
reading: Mecca was a busy trading town. People bought and sold cloth, dates and spices. Goods came in on camels. A long line of camels is called a *caravan*.
Camels can walk a long way without water. That made them good for the desert. The people of Mecca sent caravans out. Some went south in winter. Some went north in summer.
The Qur'an has a short surah about this. It is called Quraysh, surah 106. Quraysh was the name of the family group who lived in Mecca.

words.d: a long line of camels or people traveling together with things to sell

look.title: The Winter and Summer Trips
look.text: In simple words, surah 106 speaks of the people of Quraysh and the trips they made in winter and in summer. It says they should worship the Lord of the Kaaba, who gave them food and kept them safe.
look.cite: Qur'an 106:1–4, Surah Quraysh, paraphrased from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)
look.prompt: What two seasons does this surah name for the trips?

check.q: What is a caravan?
choices: A long line of camels traveling together
check.why: A caravan is a group of camels or people traveling together with goods.

check.q: Why were camels good for the desert?
choices: They can walk far without water
check.why: Camels can go a long way without drinking, which helps in a dry land.

check.q: Who were the Quraysh?
choices: The family group who lived in Mecca
check.why: Quraysh was the name of the tribe, or family group, of Mecca. Surah 106 is named for them.

lessons.title: Born Long Ago
lessons.mainIdea: Muslims say Muhammad was born in Mecca about 1,450 years ago.
reading: Muslims say *Muhammad* was born in Mecca. It was about 1,450 years ago. That is a very long time. It was long before cars, phones or lights.
Muslim tradition tells his story. Tradition means stories passed down for a long time. Muslims tell this story with love. In this course, we learn how they tell it.
Muhammad's family was part of the Quraysh. They were the people of Mecca. His father's name was Abdullah. His mother's name was Amina.

words.d: the man Muslims believe brought the words of the Qur'an; Muslims say he was born in Mecca
stories and ways that people pass down for a long time

look.title: How Long Ago?
look.cite: Rounded figures; Muhammad's birth c. 570 CE as Muslim tradition (the sira) tells it
look.prompt: Which of these happened longest ago?

check.q: Where do Muslims say Muhammad was born?
check.why: Muslim tradition says Muhammad was born in the city of Mecca.

check.q: About how long ago was Muhammad born?
check.why: Muslims say he was born about 1,450 years ago, long before cars and phones.

check.q: What does tradition mean?
choices: Stories passed down for a long time
check.why: A tradition is a story or a way of doing things that people pass down.

lessons.title: Grandfather and Uncle
lessons.mainIdea: Muhammad's parents died when he was small, so his grandfather and then his uncle cared for him.
reading: Muslim tradition says Muhammad's father died before he was born. His mother died when he was about six. A child with no living parents is an *orphan*.
His grandfather took him in. His grandfather's name was Abd al-Muttalib. Then his grandfather died too. Muhammad was about eight.
Next his uncle cared for him. His uncle's name was Abu Talib. Abu Talib kept him safe for many years. Muslims say Muhammad never forgot this care.

words.d: a child whose mother and father have died

look.title: A Verse About an Orphan
look.text: In simple words, one surah says: Did God not find you an orphan and give you a home? Muslims read these words as being about Muhammad's own childhood.
look.cite: Qur'an 93:6, Surah Ad-Duha (The Morning Hours), paraphrased from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)
look.prompt: Who do Muslims say this verse is talking about?

check.q: What is an orphan?
choices: A child whose parents have died
check.why: An orphan is a child whose mother and father have died.

check.q: Who cared for Muhammad after his grandfather died?
check.why: Muslim tradition says his uncle Abu Talib raised him after his grandfather died.

check.q: Which comes first in the story?
check.why: First his mother died, then his grandfather, and then his uncle cared for him.

lessons.title: Sheep and Quiet Places
lessons.mainIdea: As a boy, Muslims say Muhammad cared for sheep and camels and liked quiet places.
reading: Muslim tradition says Muhammad worked as a boy. He looked after sheep. He walked with them to find grass. He kept them safe from harm.
When he was older, he traveled with the caravans. He went with his uncle. He learned about camels and trading. He saw other towns.
Muslims say he liked quiet. He liked to sit alone and think. He liked the hills around Mecca. Later, this would matter a lot.

words.d: a person who takes care of sheep

look.title: A Shepherd on a Hill
look.text: Look at a boy on a rocky hill. Around him, a small flock of sheep eats dry grass. The boy holds a stick. He counts the sheep. One is walking too far away. He gets up and brings it back. Then he sits down again and looks at the sky.
look.prompt: What does a shepherd have to be good at? Name one thing.

check.q: What work did Muhammad do as a boy, in Muslim tradition?
check.why: Muslim tradition says he was a shepherd who cared for sheep as a boy.

check.q: Who did he travel with on the caravans?
check.why: Muslim tradition says he went on trading trips with his uncle Abu Talib.

check.q: What kind of places did he like?
choices: Quiet places where he could think
check.why: Muslims say he liked to be alone and think in the hills.

lessons.title: The Trustworthy
lessons.mainIdea: People in Mecca called Muhammad "the trustworthy" because he was honest.
reading: When Muhammad grew up, he worked in trade. Muslims say he was always honest. He did not cheat. He kept his word.
People in Mecca gave him a name. They called him al-Amin. That means "the *trustworthy*." A trustworthy person is one you can count on.
Muslim tradition tells a story. The Kaaba was being fixed. Families argued about a special stone. They asked Muhammad to decide. He found a fair way. Everyone was happy.

words.d: honest and safe to count on; a person who keeps their word

look.title: A Fair Way
look.text: Muslim tradition says the families argued over who would lift a special stone into the Kaaba wall. Muhammad put the stone on a cloth. Each family held a corner. They lifted it together. Then he set it in place.
look.prompt: Why did the cloth make the families stop arguing?

check.q: What does trustworthy mean?
choices: Honest, someone you can count on
check.why: A trustworthy person is honest and keeps their word.

check.q: What name did people in Mecca give Muhammad?
check.why: Muslim tradition says the people of Mecca called him al-Amin, the trustworthy.

check.q: How did Muhammad solve the argument about the stone?
choices: He had every family lift it together on a cloth
He gave it to one family
check.why: In the story, each family held a corner of the cloth, so all of them lifted the stone.

lessons.title: Khadijah
lessons.mainIdea: Muhammad married a trader named Khadijah, and Muslims remember her with honor.
reading: A woman in Mecca named *Khadijah* had a business. She sent caravans out to trade. She hired Muhammad to lead one. He did the job well.
Khadijah saw that he was honest. She asked him to marry her. He said yes. Muslims say he was about 25 years old.
They had children together. Muslims honor Khadijah very much. They say she was the first person to believe his message. You will hear that story next.

words.d: a trader in Mecca who married Muhammad; Muslims honor her as the first to believe his message

look.title: Ages in the Story
rows: The first words came, Muslims say
look.cite: Ages as Muslim tradition (the sira of Ibn Ishaq, c. 760) gives them; all are approximate
look.prompt: How many years passed between his marriage and the first words?

check.q: What was Khadijah's job?
choices: A trader who sent out caravans
check.why: Khadijah ran a trading business and sent caravans to sell goods.

check.q: Why did Khadijah want to marry Muhammad?
check.why: Muslim tradition says she chose him because he was honest and did his work well.

check.q: How do Muslims remember Khadijah?
choices: They do not talk about her
check.why: Muslims honor Khadijah as the Prophet's wife and the first to believe his message.

lessons.title: A Cave on a Mountain
lessons.mainIdea: Muhammad liked to go alone to a cave on a mountain near Mecca to think.
reading: Near Mecca is a mountain. Muslims call it the Mountain of Light. High up is a small *cave*. Its name is Hira.
Muslim tradition says Muhammad went there often. He brought food and water. He stayed for days. He sat alone and thought.
He thought about the world. He thought about right and wrong. Khadijah sent food up to him. Muslims say something big happened in that cave.

words.d: a hollow space in a hill or mountain, like a small room in the rock

look.title: Look at the Cave
look.text: Look at a small dark opening high on a rocky mountain. It is just big enough for one person to sit inside. From the opening you can see the city far below. It is very quiet. The only sound is the wind.
look.prompt: Why might a person go to a quiet place like this?

check.q: What is the name of the cave?
check.why: The cave is called Hira. It is on a mountain near Mecca.

check.q: What did Muhammad do in the cave, in Muslim tradition?
check.why: Muslim tradition says he went there to be alone and think.

check.q: Who sent food up to the cave?
check.why: Muslim tradition says his wife Khadijah made sure he had food.

review.q: What is in the middle of Mecca?
choices: The Kaaba, a building shaped like a box
review.why: The Kaaba stands in the middle of Mecca. Muslims believe it is a house for God.

review.q: How did goods come to Mecca long ago?
review.why: Camels carried goods across the desert in long lines called caravans.

review.q: Who raised Muhammad after his parents died?
review.why: Muslim tradition says his grandfather cared for him first, then his uncle Abu Talib.

review.q: Why did people call Muhammad al-Amin?
choices: Because he was honest and could be trusted
review.why: Al-Amin means the trustworthy. People said he kept his word.
Khadijah ran a trading business and married Muhammad.

review.q: Where did Muhammad go to be alone and think?
choices: A cave named Hira on a mountain
review.why: Muslim tradition says he went to the cave of Hira, near Mecca.

chapters.title: The Cave and the Word "Read"
chapters.bigQuestion: How do Muslims say the first words of the Qur'an came to Muhammad?

story.title: Wrap Me Up
story.kicker: A man runs down a dark mountain and asks his wife to cover him with a blanket.
paragraphs: It is night. The sky over Mecca is full of stars. A man is running down the side of a mountain. His heart is pounding. He is shaking. He does not stop until he gets home.
Inside the house, his wife looks up. Her name is Khadijah. "Wrap me up!" he says. "Cover me!" She brings a blanket and wraps it around him. She sits with him until the shaking stops.
Then he tells her what happened in the cave. Muslims say an angel came to him. The angel said one word: "Read!" Then it gave him words to say. He was afraid. He did not know what it meant.
Khadijah holds his hand. "You are kind. You help the poor. You tell the truth," she says. "God will not let harm come to you." This is how Muslims tell the story of the first words of the Qur'an.
story.think: Khadijah listened first and then spoke kind words. Why does that help a scared person?

lessons.title: An Angel Comes
lessons.mainIdea: Muslims believe an angel named Jibril came to Muhammad in the cave with words from God.
reading: Muhammad was in the cave of Hira. Muslims say he was about 40 years old. It was in the month of Ramadan. He was alone at night.
Muslims believe an *angel* came to him. An angel is a being Muslims believe God sends with messages. This angel's name was *Jibril*. In English, the name is Gabriel.
Muslims believe Jibril brought words from God. He told Muhammad to say them. This night is called the Night of Power. Muslims say it happened about 1,400 years ago.

words.d: a being Muslims believe God sends to bring messages to people
the angel Muslims believe brought the words of the Qur'an to Muhammad; Gabriel in English

look.title: A Night Better Than a Thousand Months
look.text: In simple words, surah 97 says God sent the Qur'an down on the Night of Power. It says that night is better than a thousand months, and that angels come down in it, and it is peace until the morning.
look.cite: Qur'an 97:1–5, Surah Al-Qadr (Power), paraphrased from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)
look.prompt: What does this surah say the angels do on that night?

check.q: Who do Muslims believe came to Muhammad in the cave?
check.why: Muslims believe the angel Jibril, or Gabriel, came with words from God.

check.q: What is an angel, as Muslims believe?
choices: A being God sends with messages
check.why: Muslims believe angels are beings God sends to bring messages.

check.q: About how old was Muhammad that night, in Muslim tradition?
check.why: Muslim tradition says he was about 40 years old when the first words came.

lessons.title: The Word "Read"
lessons.mainIdea: Muslims say the first word the angel said was "Read!", which in Arabic is Iqra.
reading: Muslims say the angel said one word first. The word was "Read!" In Arabic, it is *Iqra*. It can also mean "Say it out loud."
Muslim tradition says Muhammad answered, "I cannot read." Few people in Mecca could read then. The angel said it again. Then the angel gave him words.
Those words are in the Qur'an now. They are the first five lines of surah 96. Muslims believe they were the very first words of the whole book.

words.d: an Arabic word that means Read! or Say it out loud!; Muslims say it was the first word of the Qur'an

look.title: The First Five Lines
look.text: In simple words, surah 96 begins: Read, in the name of your Lord who made everything. He made people from a tiny clot. Read, for your Lord is most kind. He taught people to use the pen. He taught them what they did not know.
look.cite: Qur'an 96:1–5, Surah Al-'Alaq (The Clot), paraphrased from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)
look.prompt: These lines say God taught people to use something. What is it?

check.q: What does Iqra mean?
choices: Read, or say it out loud
check.why: Iqra is the Arabic word for Read! Muslims say it was the angel's first word.

check.q: Where are the first words found in the Qur'an today?
choices: At the very end of the book
check.why: Muslims say the first words are the first five lines of surah 96.

check.q: What did Muhammad answer, in Muslim tradition?
check.why: The story says he told the angel he could not read. Then the angel gave him the words.

lessons.title: Afraid and Shaking
lessons.mainIdea: Muhammad was afraid, so he ran home to Khadijah, and she comforted him.
reading: Muslim tradition says Muhammad was very *afraid*. He ran down the mountain. He went straight home. He was shaking all over.
He asked Khadijah to wrap him in a blanket. She did. She stayed by him. She did not laugh or say he was wrong. She listened.
Being afraid of something new is normal. Muslims say even the Prophet was afraid at first. What helped was a kind person who listened.

words.d: scared; feeling that something might hurt you

look.title: How the Story Was Told
look.text: A famous collection of stories about the Prophet tells it this way. In simple words: he came home with his heart pounding and said, "Cover me, cover me." They covered him until the fear left him. Then he told Khadijah, "I was afraid for myself."
look.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, the hadith on the beginning of revelation (Book of Revelation), paraphrased
look.prompt: What did Muhammad ask for first when he got home?

check.q: How did Muhammad feel after the cave, in Muslim tradition?
check.why: The story says he was afraid and shaking, and he ran home.

check.q: What did Khadijah do first?
choices: She wrapped him in a blanket
She sent him back up the mountain
check.why: She wrapped him in a blanket and stayed by him until the shaking stopped.

check.q: What helped him feel better?
check.why: Khadijah listened and spoke kind words. That is what helped.

lessons.title: Khadijah Believes
lessons.mainIdea: Muslims say Khadijah was the first person to believe that the words were from God.
reading: Khadijah told Muhammad not to fear. She said he was good to his family. He helped the poor. He told the truth. She said God would not harm such a man.
Muslims say Khadijah was the first to *believe*. To believe means to trust that something is true. She trusted that the words came from God.
One surah begins, "You who are wrapped up." Muslims say it speaks to Muhammad in his blanket. It tells him to get up.

words.d: to trust that something is true

look.title: You Who Are Wrapped Up
look.text: In simple words, surah 73 begins: You who are wrapped up in your clothes, stand up in prayer at night, for part of the night. And say the Qur'an slowly and clearly.
look.cite: Qur'an 73:1–4, Surah Al-Muzzammil (The Enshrouded One), paraphrased from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)
look.prompt: Why do Muslims connect this surah to the story of the blanket?

check.q: Who do Muslims say was the first to believe?
check.why: Muslims say Khadijah, his wife, was the first person to believe the message.

check.q: What does believe mean?
choices: To trust that something is true
check.why: To believe is to trust that something is true.

check.q: What reasons did Khadijah give that he need not fear?
choices: He was kind, helped the poor and told the truth
check.why: In the story, she names the good things he did as the reason not to be afraid.

lessons.title: Words Over Many Years
lessons.mainIdea: Muslims believe more words came to Muhammad for about 23 years, a little at a time.
reading: The words did not all come in one night. Muslims believe more came later. Sometimes a few lines came. Sometimes a whole surah came.
This went on for about 23 years. Some words came in Mecca. Later, Muhammad moved to a city called Medina. More words came there.
Muslims call the coming of these words *revelation*. Muslims believe God sent them. The words came in Arabic. They were spoken before they were written.

words.d: words Muslims believe God sent down to Muhammad through the angel Jibril

look.title: The Years of the Words
look.cite: Rounded from Muslim tradition: revelation c. 610–632 CE, the move to Medina in 622 CE
look.prompt: Where did the words come for more years, Mecca or Medina?

check.q: Did all the words of the Qur'an come in one night, as Muslims tell it?
choices: No, they came over about 23 years
No, they came over one week
check.why: Muslims believe the words came a little at a time over about 23 years.

check.q: What do Muslims call the coming of the words?
check.why: Revelation is the word for what Muslims believe God sent down to Muhammad.

check.q: What was the second city where words came?
check.why: Muslim tradition says Muhammad moved from Mecca to Medina, and words came there too.

lessons.title: Friends Learn by Heart
lessons.mainIdea: Muhammad's friends learned the words by heart and wrote them down, and they became the Qur'an.
reading: Muhammad said the words out loud. His friends listened. They said them again and again. They learned them by heart. To *memorize* is to learn by heart.
Some friends wrote the words down. There was little paper then. Muslim tradition says they wrote on leather, flat bones and stones.
After Muhammad died, Muslims say his friends gathered all the words. They put them in one book. That book is the Qur'an. Muslims still learn it by heart today.

words.d: to learn something by heart so you can say it without looking

look.title: Learning by Heart
look.text: Look at a group of friends sitting in a circle on the ground. One says a line out loud. The others say it back. They do it again. And again. Now they can say it without help. One friend scratches the words onto a flat bone with a sharp tool.
look.prompt: Have you ever learned a song by heart? How did you do it?

check.q: What does memorize mean?
check.why: To memorize is to learn something so well you can say it without looking.

check.q: What did friends write on, in Muslim tradition?
check.why: There was little paper. Tradition says they used leather, flat bones and stones.

check.q: What happened to all the words after Muhammad died?
choices: They were gathered into one book, the Qur'an
check.why: Muslims say his friends gathered the words into one book, the Qur'an.

lessons.title: What a Prophet Is
lessons.mainIdea: Muslims call Muhammad a prophet, a person who brings a message from God, and add a blessing after his name.
reading: Muslims call Muhammad a *prophet*. A prophet brings a message from God. Muslims believe there were many prophets. They say Muhammad was the last one.
When Muslims say his name, they add a blessing. They say "peace be upon him." It is a way of showing respect. You may hear a friend say it.
Jewish people and Christians also have prophets in their books. Some of the names are the same. You will meet some of them later in this course.

words.d: a person who brings a message from God, as Muslims, Jews and Christians believe

look.title: Words of Respect
look.text: Listen to a girl named Amira tell her class about her family. She says, "My grandfather reads about the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, every night." A friend asks, "Why did you say peace be upon him?" Amira says, "It is how Muslims show respect."
look.prompt: What are some ways people in your family show respect when they talk about someone?

check.q: What is a prophet?
choices: A person who brings a message from God
check.why: A prophet is a person who brings a message from God, as these faiths believe.

check.q: What do Muslims add after Muhammad's name?
check.why: Muslims say "peace be upon him" after his name to show respect.

check.q: Who else has prophets in their books?
check.why: Jewish people and Christians also have prophets, and some names are shared.

review.q: What is the name of the angel in the story, as Muslims tell it?
review.why: Muslims believe the angel Jibril, called Gabriel in English, came to the cave.

review.q: What was the angel's first word, in Muslim tradition?
review.why: Muslims say the first word was Iqra, which means Read!

review.q: What did Muhammad ask Khadijah to do when he got home?
review.why: He was shaking and asked to be covered with a blanket.

review.q: About how many years did the words keep coming, as Muslims believe?
review.why: Muslims believe revelation continued for about 23 years.

review.q: How did Muhammad's friends keep the words?
choices: They learned them by heart and wrote them down
review.why: Friends memorized the words and wrote some on leather, bones and stones.

choices: A person who brings a message from God
review.why: A prophet brings a message from God, as Muslims, Jews and Christians believe.
